chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated that Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Husayni quoted on the authority of Isa ibn Mihran, on the authority of Abu Salt Abdul Salam ibn Salih, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha', on the authority of his father Musa, on the authority of his father Ja'far, on the authority of his father Muhammad, on the authority of his father Ali ibn Al-Husayn, on the authority of his father Al-Husayn, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
If a man cannot pray standing up, he should pray sitting down. If he cannot pray sitting down, he should pray lying on his back with his legs stretched out toward the Qibla, gesturing with a nod.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to pray if one cannot stand or sit?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the pristine chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, establishes the legal principle of *tadrij* (gradual accommodation) in prayer, ensuring that physical limitations do not invalidate the act of worship. It specifically highlights the *mustalqi* posture—lying on the back with legs facing the Qibla—as the final resort, a detail often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of gestures for those with severe mobility issues.
